# Feature: Glass tile — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #46 (Glass tile) from Terrain and Hazards before it is used in real levels. Effect: cracks, breaks on second crossing. Unique: allows exactly one return crossing, unlike crumbling. Useful: a there-and-back-once route over a drop. Source status in the candidate file is 'trial'.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** cracks, breaks on second crossing.

**So that** a there-and-back-once route over a drop.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Glass tile for the first time in its teaching room (mech-46-glass-tile-room). Teaching moment: First room: a glass tile over a drop, with an orb on the far side and a key visible beyond it. A player who crosses for the orb and comes straight back uses the second crossing without realising it was the last one the glass would allow, and must find another way to the key, which teaches that glass allows a return exactly once. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: First crossing cracks it
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: The second crossing, in either direction, shatters it after you leave and it becomes a void tile
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Standing on a cracked tile is safe

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.
- No soft-lock: every reachable state has a legal move, a lose, or a reset.
- Definition audit: glass: tile over a drop defined here; first crossing cracks it, second crossing is the last it allows
- Definition audit: void: hole after the glass shatters, per mechanic 5 in this file; entering it is falling
- Definition audit: drop: open space below the glass, treated exactly as void per mechanic 5 in this file

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Glass tile's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Testing

Needs a mechanics playground: new — Test Level mech-46-glass-tile-room, built from this mechanic's teaching moment above. What to check there: every rule in Player-Facing Behavior, played in mech-46-glass-tile-room; the teaching moment's first (naive) action should fail as described and the corrected action should succeed. Record play sessions for replay: yes — sessions are the review evidence. Synergy rooms are explicitly deferred to a later run and are not part of this feature's check.
Named test cases (from the candidate file; all must be played):
- Test case there and back exactly once: first crossing cracks the glass, the return crossing crosses safely, and leaving it the second time shatters it to void
- Test case adversarial third approach: after shattering, pressing toward the void is blocked; an alternate route or restart resolves the room, never a stranded tile
- Test case safe standing on cracked glass: standing and turning on cracked glass does not shatter it; only leaving after the second crossing does
- Test case restart and replay: restart restores intact glass, and a recorded session replays to the same end state
